{{Short description|German evolutionary ecologist}}
'''Martin Kaltenpoth''' (born in 1977 in [[Hagen]]) is a German evolutionary ecologist.

== Scientific career ==
After studying [[biology]] at the [[University of Würzburg]], which was supported by the German Academic Scholarship Foundation ([[Studienstiftung]]), Kaltenpoth completed his doctorate in 2006 under the supervision of Erhard Strohm on the topic ''Protective bacteria and attractive pheromones - symbiosis and chemical communication in beewolves''.<ref>[https://opus.bibliothek.uni-wuerzburg.de/frontdoor/index/index/year/2006/docId/1775 Online Publication Service of Würzburg University]</ref> He was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Regensburg]] and the [[University of Utah]] in [[Salt Lake City]]. In 2009, he joined the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Ecology]] as head of the Max Planck Research Group Insect Symbiosis. In 2015, he was appointed Chair of Evolutionary Ecology at the [[University of Mainz]]. Since 2020, he has been Director and Scientific Member at the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Ecology]] and Head of the Department of Insect Symbiosis.<ref>[https://www.mpg.de/14608616/chemical-ecology-kaltenpoth Profile on the webpage of the Max Planck Society]</ref>

== Research ==
Kaltenpoth studies symbioses between insects and microorganisms. Bacteria are important partners for their hosts, as they help open up new habitats and the exploit new food sources.<ref>[https://idw-online.de/en/news749276 Versatile symbionts: Reed beetles benefit from bacterial helpers through all life stages, press release, Dec. 6, 2020]</ref> They also play a vital role in their host insects’ defense against enemies.<ref>[https://idw-online.de/en/news766914 Defensive symbiosis leads to gene loss in bacterial partners, press release, Appr. 19, 2021]</ref> The goal of Kaltenpoth's research is to characterize the diversity of bacterial symbionts in insects and their importance for the ecology of their hosts, tracing their evolutionary origin.<ref>[https://idw-online.de/en/news689071 Beewolves have been successfully using the same antibiotics for 68 million years, press release, Feb. 13, 2018]</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
* Student Research Grant Award, Animal Behavior Society, USA, 2001
* Theodore Roosevelt Memorial Grant, [[American Museum of Natural History]], USA, 2002
* Biocenter Science Award of the [[University of Würzburg]], 2006
* Award of the Ingrid Weiss / Horst Wiehe Foundation, German Society for General and Applied Entomology (DGaaE), 2007<ref>[https://www.dgaae.de/de/i-weiss-h-wiehe-stiftung.html Förderpreis der Ingrid Weiss / Horst Wiehe Stiftung]</ref>
* Young Scientist Award, [[Society for Experimental Biology]] (SEB), United Kingdom, 2007
* Thuringian Science Award of the Thuringian Ministry for Economy, Science and Digital Society, Germany, 2014<ref>[https://www.welt.de/regionales/thueringen/article138196333/20-Thueringer-Forschungspreis-geht-an-vier-Institute.html 20. Thüringer Forschungspreis geht an vier Institute]</ref>
* Griswold Lecture, Department of Entomology, [[Cornell University]], USA, 2018
* European Research Council (ERC) Consolidator Grant, 2019<ref>[https://idw-online.de/en/news708414 ERC Consolidator Grant for research on the relationship between beetles and symbiotic bacteria, press release, Dec. 6, 2018]</ref>
* Elected Member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]], 2023<ref>[https://www.embo.org/press-releases/embo-announces-election-of-new-members/ EMBO announces election of new members, EMBO Communications, July 4, 2023]</ref>
* Honorary Professorship for Evolutionary Ecology at [[University of Jena]], Faculty of Biosciences, 2023,<ref>[https://www.ice.mpg.de/457213/Martin-Kaltenpoth-honorary-professor Martin Kaltenpoth appointed honorary professor at Friedrich Schiller University, October 30, 2023]</ref>
